topics.topic: Owner and staff actor distinction, membership, trust, and exclusive privileges
questions: Are owner and staff one actor, or distinct actors; if distinct, who qualifies as staff and which privileges belong only to the owner besides changing configuration?
Who counts as staff besides the owner, and what trust distinguishes staff from the owner who alone administers the host, vault and configuration?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about owner/staff identity and credential-based privileges already judged in P1.

precedent.topic: Definition and permissions of owner and staff actors
quotes:
Each writing service holds a service token that names it; staff hold a staff
credential. Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or
erasing a customer needs the staff credential.
How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend.

how a credential's holder is checked against the 'who'
of each action, and what each service token may do;
precedent.why: The authentication rule that determines whether possession of a credential qualifies its holder for an action is explicitly carried to State 2.

topics.topic: Whether model providers are authorized recipients despite the staff-only contact-data rule
questions: Are model providers authorized recipients of customer contact data, or does “readable by staff only” prohibit disclosure to anyone outside staff?
Does “readable by staff only” describe only API authorization, or must model providers also be recognized as authorized external recipients of customer contact data?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about model-provider receipt of staff-only contact data already answered in P2.

precedent.topic: Whether staff-only contact data may be disclosed to external model providers
quotes:
Name, phone, e-mail and language are
all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09),
and erasable as a whole.

every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the
model the owner runs it on — today Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for
Codex — under that provider's own terms. Registry does not limit which
fields or which provider, and the owner accepts this (owner, 2026-10-27).
precedent.why: The text explicitly permits an operator acting as staff to pass contact data to the owner's model provider, so staff-only describes Registry access rather than an absolute ban on downstream disclosure.

topics.topic: Whether an operator agent may access the store, configuration, and service tokens
questions: Is an operator agent authorized to read the store, configuration and service tokens through the owner's host access, or are those resources restricted to the human owner and Registry process?

topics.topic: Whether model providers may receive store contents, configuration, and service tokens
questions: When an agent uses host access, may store contents, configuration and service tokens pass to its model provider, or is provider exposure accepted only for customer contact fields?

topics.topic: Whether onboard_object can run directly without a model agent or provider disclosure
questions: Does every use of `onboard_object` necessarily run through a model agent and disclose contact data to a model provider, or can the script be used directly without that disclosure?

topics.topic: Who holds the Registry frontend staff credential and whether the browser is within the secrets boundary
questions: For a Registry frontend running in a browser on Registry’s host, which actor holds and presents the staff credential, and is that browser inside the secrets trust boundary?
